en.title: Val d'Isère snow forecast: fresh snow returns next week, 28 cm at the top (23–29 November 2026)
en.description: Val d'Isère gets 28 cm next week (10–46 cm range) with Thursday 26 November as the peak snowfall day. Forecast from 16 November 2026.
en.lede: Next week Val d'Isère receives a solid dose of fresh snow across all heights, with the upper slopes collecting around 28 cm and the base nearly as much. Thursday 26 November delivers the heaviest fall—a day worth timing your visit around if you can choose.

sections.h: What lands where across next week
p: The week of 23–29 November spreads snow unevenly. Upper slopes around 3200 m gather 28 cm (the range: 10–46 cm), mid-mountain around 2600 m receives 26 cm (9–42 cm), and the base at 1900 m takes 24 cm (9–38 cm).

Three days drive most of the total. Wednesday 25 November adds 6 cm at the top, Thursday 26 adds the bulk at 10 cm (up to 16 cm), and Sunday 29 wraps the week with another 6 cm (up to 12 cm). The days between are nearly dry.

sections.h: Where to find the best snow
p: Aim for the Pissaillas glacier and the exposed tops of Solaise and Bellevarde, where depth accumulates fastest. If you want soft snow, Bellevarde's east and north-facing flanks above La Daille hold shade through the week and keep the surface from crusting.

Lower down, the long run-out paths to La Daille and the village are your safety net. If the air warms mid-week, these lower slopes feel it first, so check the village-level forecast if you plan to ski base-to-base.

sections.h: Before next week: this week's setup
p: Before the main event, Val d'Isère is already deep. From Tuesday 17 to Friday 20 November, the upper mountain holds 83 cm (67–99 cm). The base at that point sits at 46 cm. This first storm lays the groundwork for next week's fresh layer to bond well.
By Friday 20, you are sitting on a solid base. The second storm then adds 28 cm on top of an already-safe foundation.

sections.h: Timing matters more than the total
p: The forecast range (10–46 cm at the top) is wide because a week is still far away. But the timing of Thursday 26 November is reliable: that is when the snow gun points at Val d'Isère. Plan for Thursday and Friday to hold the best powder, with Sunday 29 offering a second chance if weather shifts.
The closer days (Tuesday, Wednesday) are more certain than the far end of the week (Sunday onwards), so if the forecast shifts, watch for changes to the Thursday peak first.

Tignes (6 km away) gets 29 cm next week, Les Arcs (19 km away) also 29 cm, and La Plagne (23 km away) tops out at 28 cm. Val d'Isère ties with La Plagne and runs only 1 cm behind Tignes and Les Arcs—a rounding difference.
If one resort thins out or warms faster mid-week, Val d'Isère shares the Espace Killy with Tignes, so you can cross over. The choice between resorts rests on terrain and your skill, not snow depth.

sections.h: What to do before you go
p: Check the French avalanche bulletin (BERA) for the massif: a fresh snowpack this young can slide. Confirm the resort's opening date and which lifts are running—snow on the slopes and open lifts are not the same thing.
Watch the midweek forecast carefully. If the range tightens or shifts, the top can swing by 36 cm (from 10 to 46), so a low forecast midweek means you may want to delay by a day or two.

advice: Thursday 26 and Friday 27 November: aim for these two days if you can. Thursday is the peak snowfall day; Friday is when the new snow is set and rideable.
Fresh snow on a young base: before any off-piste skiing, read the BERA avalanche bulletin for your massif and ride with someone who knows the terrain.
Height matters. Stick to 2600 m and above next week to find the most reliable snow; lower slopes risk rain or crust if the air warms.
Bellevarde's shaded flanks and the Pissaillas glacier will hold the best quality. Plan your itinerary there for Thursday afternoon or Friday morning.
If the base forecast thins to the low end (10 cm at the top), cross to Tignes to test the Espace Killy's deeper side before committing to lower runs.
